$\mathcal P_i$ be [[def-minimal-parabolic-klr-diagram-proof-category]], with
its homogeneous polynomial realization and PBW/bubble normal form. Fix monic
$a_j(u)=u^{\lambda_j}+\sum_{r<\lambda_j}c_{j,r}u^r$; for the standard graded
cyclotomic quotient take $a_j(u)=u^{\lambda_j}$ as in
[[def-cyclotomic-klr-quotient-at-a-dominant-weight]]. More generally first take
universal graded coefficients of degree $2d_j(\lambda_j-r)$; arbitrary monic
specializations over the field are interpreted as ungraded.

**Given:** A dominant $\Lambda$, the formal category $\mathcal P_i$ of
[[def-minimal-parabolic-klr-diagram-proof-category]] with its model and normal

matchings, dot monomials and independent far-left bubble monomials form a
basis; specializing the central vacuum bubble coefficients alone gives the
all-downward corner $R(\beta)$ with its ordinary polynomial/crossing part
unchanged.

For the standard homogeneous first-strand cyclotomic quotient over any field
and every homogeneous (Q1)-(Q4) datum, use basic right-append induction $F_i$
from $\beta$ to $\beta+\alpha_i$ and basic restriction $E_i$ in the reverse
direction. Put $h=\langle h_i,\Lambda-\beta\rangle$ and
$t_i(\beta)=2d_i(1-h)=(\alpha_i\mid\alpha_i)-2(\Lambda-\beta\mid\alpha_i)$.
Then there are explicit homogeneous bimodule units and counits with both
triangle identities giving $E_i\{t_i(\beta)\}\dashv F_i\dashv E_i$ on all
graded module categories. They preserve the standard dot-cyclic and same-color
crossing-mate identities and the coherent different-color double-mate
identity: for $p_\nu=\tau_re(\nu)$ with bottom adjacent colors $(i,j)$,
$i\ne j$, its double right mate is $(t_{ji}/t_{ij})p_\nu$, where $t_{ij}$ is
the coefficient of $u^{-a_{ij}}$ in $Q_{ij}(u,v)$ and the strand of color $i$
runs SW to NE. Equivalently the associated right closure satisfies
$\operatorname{cl}(p_\nu a)=(t_{ji}/t_{ij})\operatorname{cl}(ap_\nu)$ for
$a\in e(\nu)R^\Lambda(\beta)e(s_r\nu)$; dots, idempotents and equal-color
crossings have ratio $1$. The corresponding arbitrary monic field quotients
have the same underlying ungraded biadjunction and ordered crossing-mate
identities after forgetting internal shifts. No Frobenius, integral
Grothendieck-module or crystal theorem is a premise.

[F1] The formal category relations and their graded flag-model realization:
triangles, rank-one matrices with inverses, mixed dot compatibility,
cross-and-cap identities and normalized bubble slides
([[def-minimal-parabolic-klr-diagram-proof-category]],
[[lem-minimal-parabolic-polynomial-flag-model-realizes-the-graded-diagram-relations]],
[[lem-minimal-parabolic-diagrams-have-pbw-bubble-normal-form]]).

[F2] The cap-off identification
([[lem-cyclotomic-cap-off-quotient-has-no-extra-downward-relations]]): the
cyclotomic quotient corner is the downward-word Hom corner of
$\mathcal P_i(\Lambda)/J$, with composition corresponding to multiplication.

**Proof technique:** transport the model-verified formal cups, caps and mates
through the cap-off identification, keeping all degrees in the declared grading,
and read the biadjunction and the mate ratios off the explicit coefficient
traces.

2.1 The explicit units and counits. At a vertex with $r$ $i$-roots and total monic degree $N$ put $L=C[e_1,\dots,e_r]/(\text{factor coefficients above }N-r)$, $c_r=\prod(u-x_a)$, $p=a_i\prod_{j\ne i}Q_{ij}/t_{ij}$ and $b=p/c_r$. The $i$-flag algebra is $B=L[z]/b(z)$, free over the old ring on the powers $0\le j<N-r$ and free over the target root-append ring on the powers $0\le j\le r$. The two coefficient traces $\tau_{\mathrm{old}}$ and $\tau_{\mathrm{new}}$ extract the respective top powers of the monic remainders, and their Gram matrices in the power/complementary bases are triangular with diagonal $1$, so they have explicit dual bases without factorial denominators. Basic $F_i=B\{-2d_ir\}\otimes-$ and basic reverse $E_i=B\otimes-$ use $\tau_{\mathrm{new}}$ and its dual bases; the second adjunction $E_i\{t_i(\beta)\}\dashv F_i$ uses $\tau_{\mathrm{old}}$ in the same way. Restricting the model equations of [F1] through the cap-off identification [F2] gives homogeneous units and counits with both triangle identities, hence $E_i\{t_i(\beta)\}\dashv F_i\dashv E_i$. [step 1.1, F1, F2]

3.1 Crossing mates. The model's rank-one rho and cross-and-cap equations of [F1] identify the two adjunction mates of a crossing with the same normalizations used in the formal definition; on the $i,j$ pair the successive rings are $D_1=L_m[y,z]/(b(z)q_{ij}(z,y))$ and $D_0=L_m[y,z]/b(z)$, and the normalized opposite-sideways composites have scalars $t_{ij}$ and $t_{ji}$, with double right mate $(t_{ji}/t_{ij})p_\nu$ in the stated source orientation. Dots, idempotents and equal-color crossings have ratio $1$ by dot-cyclicity and the equal-color mixed relations. Reading these model identities through the cap-off isomorphism [F2] proves the stated mate identities in $R^\Lambda$, and the same transported identities hold verbatim after arbitrary monic specialization with shifts forgotten. [step 2.1, F1, F2]

4.1 Conclusion. Steps 2.1 and 3.1 establish the graded biadjunction $E_i\{t_i(\beta)\}\dashv F_i\dashv E_i$ and the ordered crossing-mate identities with their exact scalars, using only the model-verified relations, the cap-off identification and the projective comparison of [F3]; no Frobenius, integral Grothendieck-module or crystal statement is used as a premise. [step 3.1, F3] ∎

For the standard first-strand cyclotomic quotient of a real symmetrizable KLR
datum over any degree-zero field and every homogeneous (Q1)–(Q4) parameter
family, put $A=R^\Lambda(\beta)$, $B=R^\Lambda(\beta+\alpha_i)$,
$e=e(\beta,i)$, $X=Be$, $Y=eB$,
$h=\langle h_i,\Lambda-\beta\rangle$ and $t=2d_i(1-h)$.
There are explicit, compatible homogeneous maps
$$T_i:eBe\longrightarrow A,\qquad \deg T_i=t,$$
and finite homogeneous tensors
$$C_i=\sum_\alpha x_\alpha\otimes_A y_\alpha\in X\otimes_A Y,\qquad \deg x_\alpha+\deg y_\alpha=-t,$$
such that $T_i$ is an $A$-bimodule map, $bC_i=C_ib$ for every $b\in B$, and
$$x=\sum_\alpha x_\alpha T_i(y_\alpha x),\qquad y=\sum_\alpha T_i(yx_\alpha)y_\alpha.$$
In particular $X\{t\}\cong\operatorname{HOM}_A(Y,A)$ as $(B,A)$-bimodules,
where Hom is left-$A$-linear, the left $B$-action is precomposition with
right multiplication on $Y$, and the right $A$-action is multiplication on
values. The second unit is $b\mapsto bC_i$ and the second counit is
$y\otimes_B x\mapsto T_i(yx)$, giving
$E_i\{t\}\dashv F_i\dashv E_i$ on all graded modules. They are obtained by
finite normal-form/cap transport, not by assuming an actual Frobenius trace.
Dots and same-color crossing mates have the native cyclic normalization.
Each specified distinguished-$i$ different-color sideways pair has both
composites $t_{ij}$ times the identity. The separately distinguished-$j$
construction has both composites $t_{ji}$ times the identity. These are
different partial actions, not two different scalar values for the two
orders of one pair; their full word-closure comparison is not inferred here.
Arbitrary monic field specializations have the same ungraded construction,
with grading shifts forgotten. No finite-type, characteristic-zero,
geometric-global-basis or symmetric-trace premise is used.

[F1] The fully typed formal category and its independently constructed
flag inverse/cap maps
([[def-minimal-parabolic-klr-diagram-proof-category]],
[[lem-cyclotomic-polynomial-flag-comparison-has-the-prescribed-second-mate-inverse]]):
both rank-one inverse equations, both formal adjunction triangles,
dot/same-color cyclicity, and the normalized partial different-color mate
pairs. At outside weight $h$ the first unit and second counit have degree
$s=d_i(1-h)$; at the adjacent outside weight $h-2$ the first counit and
second unit have degree $-s$. The same distinguished-$i$ pair has both
composites $t_{ij}$; the separately distinguished-$j$ construction has
scalar $t_{ji}$.

[F2] The normal-form/cap-ideal supplier
([[lem-oriented-minimal-parabolic-klr-normal-forms-and-cyclotomic-cap-ideal-intersection]]):
the quotient representable category has the exact cyclotomic downward Hom
corners, its ideal is stable under all allowed whiskers, and every mixed
word is a retract of a finite sum of downward words by its specified
finite rank-one reduction. No extra downward relation occurs. Its corner
identifications respect composition, word idempotents and generator
append maps, also for arbitrary monic specializations.

7.1 Native compatibility and the two partial constructions. All transformations were transported through a fully faithful equivalence preserving append generators and the first adjunction. Therefore the actual dot and same-color mate equations are exactly the realized equations of [F1], with $\kappa=-\tau$ throughout. For the $i$-partial different-color pair, its maps are the concrete cup--$\kappa_{ij}$--cap and opposite cup--$\kappa_{ji}$--cap contractions in [F1]; both composites are $t_{ij}$ times their respective identities. Passing to native crossings negates each of these single-crossing maps, so the two signs cancel in either composite. Repeating the entire construction with distinguished color $j$ gives its actual pair with scalar $t_{ji}$ in both orders. This proves the stated partial mate compatibilities at their actual source/target weights, without identifying an $H_j$ inside $\mathcal P_i$, which contains only $H_i$. A full word-closure comparison between the two separately constructed partial actions requires an additional calculation. [step 1.1, step 2.1, step 3.1, F1, algebra]

Fix a color $i$. In the formal graded minimal-parabolic proof category of
[[def-minimal-parabolic-klr-diagram-proof-category]], the reduced
perfect-matching diagrams, dot monomials on their open components, and
monomials in the independent far-left normalized $i$-bubble coefficients form
a basis of every morphism space. In particular, at all-downward boundaries of
weight difference $\beta$, the morphism space is the corresponding KLR PBW
corner tensored with the polynomial ring in one positive bubble family; the
opposite/fake family is its coefficientwise reciprocal. The graded polynomial
flag models of
[[lem-minimal-parabolic-polynomial-flag-model-realizes-the-graded-diagram-relations]],
with universal monic framing and arbitrarily large auxiliary framing at each
fixed physical source weight, are jointly faithful. The assertion is about this
formal proof category before cyclotomic quotient transfer.

**Given:** The formal graded minimal-parabolic proof category
$\mathcal P_i$ of [[def-minimal-parabolic-klr-diagram-proof-category]] for a
fixed color $i$, with its generators, graded shifts and relations.

[F1] The relations of $\mathcal P_i$ are the model-verified local equations of
[[lem-minimal-parabolic-polynomial-flag-model-realizes-the-graded-diagram-relations]]:
downward KLR relations, both rank-one triangles with cyclic dots, the
rho/cross-and-cap equations, bubble inversion, the mixed cap/cup equations and
the finite-coefficient bubble slides; the polynomial flag models realize all of
them.

1.1 Bubble slides on the model. For an $i$ root $x$ the normalized bubble series changes by $(1-xt)^{\pm2}$, and for a spectator $j$ root $y$ it changes by $q_{ij}^{\mathrm{rev}}(y,t)^{\pm1}$ with $q_{ij}^{\mathrm{rev}}=t^{-a_{ij}}Q_{ij}(t^{-1},y)/t_{ij}$ of constant coefficient $1$. These hold directly because the model series is $p^{\mathrm{rev}}/(c_r^{\mathrm{rev}})^2$, adjoining an $i$ root multiplies $c_r$ by $u-x$, and adjoining a spectator root multiplies $p$ by $Q_{ij}/t_{ij}$; every fixed inverse coefficient is a finite polynomial recursion. These are the specified formal relations, checked on the model and not derived from the faithfulness being proved. [F1, algebra]

4.1 Independence by degree separation. Fix the physical source weight $\mu$ and write $\mu_i=\langle h_i,\mu\rangle$; choose spectator background counts $m_j$ with $A_{\mathrm{spect}}=\sum_{j\ne i}(-a_{ij})m_j$ and for an increasing background $i$-count $r$ set $N=\mu_i+2r$, $\lambda_i=N-A_{\mathrm{spect}}$, so the physical weight $N-2r=\mu_i$ is fixed. Use the universal monic framing $a_i(u)=u^{\lambda_i}+z_1u^{\lambda_i-1}+\cdots+z_{\lambda_i}$ with independent $\deg z_a=2d_ia$, put $p=a_i\prod_{j\ne i}Q_{ij}/t_{ij}$ and $c_r=\prod_a(u-x_a)$; the normalized series $\mathcal B(t)=p^{\mathrm{rev}}/(c_r^{\mathrm{rev}})^2=a_i^{\mathrm{rev}}U(t)$ with $U_0=1$ has coefficients $\mathcal B_a=z_a+\sum_{1\le\ell<a}z_\ell U_{a-\ell}+U_a$, unit triangular in the framing variables, with reciprocal coefficients $-z_a$ plus lower framing indices. Hence the first $D$ bubble coefficients are independent whenever $\lambda_i\ge D$, in every characteristic and at every physical weight; no unit old-root coefficient is claimed, since $\mathcal B_1=p_1+2e_1$ can lose its root term in characteristic two. A nonzero finite PBW/bubble combination remains nonzero after this triangular substitution over the independent polynomial coefficient domain; the generic KLR polynomial representation has a distinct nonzero leading permutation for each selected crossing word, so a polynomial test vector with nonzero output exists after clearing a finite denominator. Let $D$ bound the bubble indices and $B$ the actual internal degrees of that vector and its output, both finite in the untruncated polynomial ring, and let $L$ bound the number of added $i$-flags tested. Every monic flag relation and factor-ring coefficient relation after those flags has degree at least $2d_i(\mu_i+r-L+1)$, spectator appends only increase $N$, all variables are nonnegatively graded and all dot degrees are positive; choosing $r\ge0$ and $\lambda_i\ge D$ with $2d_i(\mu_i+r-L+1)>B$ (possible at fixed $\mu$) separates all model relations from degree $\le B$, so the nonzero PBW output survives in that flag model. [step 3.1, F1]

Fix a color $i$ and the formal proof category of
[[def-minimal-parabolic-klr-diagram-proof-category]], on a symmetrizable real
Cartan datum with finite index set and arbitrary field $k$. Use the native KLR
parameters of
[[def-quiver-hecke-klr-algebra-for-a-symmetrizable-cartan-datum]], degrees of
[[def-klr-grading-and-diagrammatic-composition]], the PBW convention of
[[thm-klr-pbw-basis-theorem]], and the nil-Hecke matrix/idempotent convention
of [[def-divided-power-klr-idempotents-and-projectives]]. Then the polynomial
flag construction described below realizes all the defining graded diagram
relations of that formal category, including its rank-one cross/cap,
bubble-slide/inversion and mixed-color cup/cap relations; it asserts a
representation of the formal proof category, not faithfulness or a cyclotomic
quotient identification.

**The model.** Choose a color order with $i$ last. For spectator alphabets
$Y_j$ of sizes $m_j$ ($j\ne i$) put $C=\bigotimes_{j\ne i}k[Y_j]^{S_{m_j}}$,
$r=m_i$, $A_{ij}=-a_{ij}$,
$t_{ij}=[u^{A_{ij}}]Q_{ij}(u,v)\in k^\times$,
$q_{ij}=Q_{ij}/t_{ij}$, and choose a monic framing polynomial $a_i(u)$ of
degree $\lambda_i$; initially its coefficients have their universal homogeneous
degrees, so all formulas are graded, and the standard specialization is
$a_i(u)=u^{\lambda_i}$. Set
$$p_m(u)=a_i(u)\prod_{j\ne i}\prod_{y\in Y_j}q_{ij}(u,y),\qquad N=\lambda_i+\sum_{j\ne i}A_{ij}m_j,\qquad h_m=N-2r,$$
and $c_r(u)=u^r-e_1u^{r-1}+\cdots+(-1)^re_r$. The vertex ring $L_m$ is the
monic factor ring for $p_m=c_rb_{N-r}$, equivalently $C[e_1,\ldots,e_r]$ modulo
all coefficients beyond degree $N-r$ of the monic expansion $p_m/c_r$; it is
finite free over $C$ of rank $\binom Nr$ and is zero for $r>N$. Its $i$ flag is
$B_m=L_m[z]/b_{N-r}(z)$, free of rank $N-r$ over $L_m$ and rank $r+1$ over
$L_{m+i}$, with the target root alphabet obtained by adjoining $z$. The
underlying spectator flag is $C_m^j=L_m[y]$; its target action appends $y$ to
$Y_j$ and replaces $p_m$ by $p_mq_{ij}(u,y)$.

**Crossings, colors and bubbles.** Source crossings are
$\kappa=-\tau_{\mathrm{native}}$ for EVERY color pair. Source equal-color
operators are $(s-1)/(X-Y)$; source unequal operators are the switch/quotient
in the increasing-color direction and switch times $Q$ in the reverse
direction. Thus native operators are their negatives, and both actual crossing
degrees are $-b_{jk}$ with the ordered shifts above. On the $i,j$ pair the
successive underlying rings are
$D_1=L_m[y,z]/(b(z)q_{ij}(z,y))$ and $D_0=L_m[y,z]/b(z)$, with source maps
$\pi:D_1\to D_0$ and $f\mapsto Q_{ij}(z,y)f:D_0\to D_1$; their normalized
opposite-sideways composites have the scalars $t_{ij}$ and $t_{ji}$, and in the
NE/SW-$i$, NW/SE-$j$ source orientation the double-mate ratio is
$t_{ji}/t_{ij}$. Native minus signs leave the two-crossing scalars and the
ratio unchanged. The basic isomorphism $E_iG_j\cong(G_jE_i)\{-b_{ij}\}$ holds,
and the normalized formal $H_iG_j\cong G_jH_i$ is unshifted.

**Given:** The formal proof category of [[def-minimal-parabolic-klr-diagram-proof-category]]; the native KLR datum $Q$ and its degrees; a fixed color $i$; the monic framing polynomial $a_i$ and the spectator alphabets $Y_j$.

3.1 The four coefficient maps and their triangles. For a monic $f$, the polynomial kernel $K_f(X,Y)=(f(X)-f(Y))/(X-Y)$ is defined before imposing $f(X)=f(Y)=0$ and satisfies $(X-Y)K_f=f(X)-f(Y)$ and $\tau_XK_f=1$; therefore $\tau_X(X^aK_f)=Y^a$ for every $a$, which identifies $K_f$ with the dual-power-basis Casimir of the two monic coefficient forms. The two Casimirs of $b_{N-r}$ and $c_{r+1}$ give the four displayed cups and caps; their contractions are the identities $\sum_av_a\tau(z^ab)=b$ and $\sum_a\tau(bv_a)z^a=b$ for dual Artin bases, and substituting them into the tensor composites proves both triangles of each of the two adjunctions. Degrees: $\tau_{\mathrm{old}}$ extracts $z^{N-r-1}$ and has degree $-2d_i(N-r-1)$; $\tau_{\mathrm{new}}$ extracts $z^r$ and has degree $-2d_ir$; the first maps have degree $0$ after the $B\{-2d_ir\}$ shift; the second cap has degree $-2d_i(N-r-1)+2d_ir=-2d_i(h_m-1)$, with inverse degree on its unit. Restoring the normalized $H_i$ at its input weight produces exactly the four formal degrees of [[def-minimal-parabolic-klr-diagram-proof-category]]. [step 2.1, algebra]

5.1 Same-color crossing, curl and bubble identities. Equal crossings act by $\kappa=(s-1)/(X-Y)$, so $\kappa^2=0$, the braid relation holds and the two mixed dot equations follow from the rational divided-difference expansion; $K_f$ is symmetric, so its divided-difference correction vanishes and $(X-Y)K_f=f(X)-f(Y)$ gives the dot-mate equations. Contracting a crossing against either Casimir and using the rank-one block inverse of step 4.1 produces the cross-and-cap/curl equations: expanding $(f(X)-f(Y))/(X-Y)$ in the power bases and taking the top-coefficient rows gives the four signed sums over $a+b=-1$ and $a+b+c=-2$ with the stated orientation signs. The resulting oriented bubble Laurent series is $\Phi_i(u)=p_m(u)/c_r(u)^2$ of leading degree $h_m=N-2r$; its reciprocal is the opposite series with product $1$ coefficient by coefficient, forced by composing the two flag coefficient pairings, since each existing $i$ root contributes one factor from each side of the cap. Appending an $i$ root $z$ changes $\Phi_i$ to $\Phi_i/(u-z)^2$ and appending a spectator $j$ root $y$ changes it to $\Phi_iQ_{ij}(u,y)/t_{ij}$; expanding at infinity gives every finite bubble-slide coefficient equation. At a monic vacuum, $a_i(x)x^{\ell-1}=0$ gives $h_\ell+\sum_jc_{\lambda_i-j}h_{\ell-j}=0$ with $h_0=1$, $h_{<0}=0$, so $H(t)a_i^{\mathrm{rev}}(t)=1$. All coefficients use only addition, multiplication and monic formal inversion. [step 3.1, step 4.1, algebra]

6.1 Downward $Q$-relations and exact word grading. Give every flag the ordered shift $s_j(m)$ of the Statement. For $j<k$ the increasing word $(j,k)$ maps to the word $(k,j)$ by a quotient/switch of underlying degree $0$, with target-minus-source unit shift $-b_{jk}$; the reverse operator has underlying degree $-2b_{jk}$ and unit-shift $+b_{jk}$, so both have actual degree $-b_{jk}$, and same-color divided differences have degree $-2d_j$. Native operators are the negatives of the source operators, so their degrees and two-crossing composites are unchanged. The ordinary polynomial operators satisfy the idempotent, dot, far-commutation and quadratic $Q$-relations directly; expanding a three-strand composition gives zero difference for distinct outer colors and the divided difference of $Q$ for equal outer colors, and the global substitution $\kappa=-\tau$ changes all cubic signs to the native numerator. The quotient relations descend: on an $i,j$ pair $D_1$ has $bq=0$ and $D_0$ has $b=0$, and $Qb=t_{ij}bq$ makes multiplication by $Q$ well defined while the other crossing is the literal quotient. [step 2.1, step 3.1, step 5.1, algebra]

6.2 Mixed cups and caps with their constants. In $D[z]/p$ versus $D[z]/(pq)$ the coefficient form satisfies $\tau_{pq}(Qf)=t_{ij}\tau_p(f)$, because $Q=t_{ij}q$ and the leading coefficient of $Qf$ is $t_{ij}$ times that of $f$. For a full existing $i$-string use the ordered residue form $t_r^p(z)=(-1)^{r(N-r)}\operatorname{Res}\bigl(\Delta_r(X)X_1^{r-1}\cdots X_{r-1}\operatorname{Tr}(z)/\prod_ap(X_a)\bigr)$, in which no $1/r!$ occurs; expanding parabolic divided differences verifies this over the universal integral coefficient ring, and over its generic-root fraction field the sum over root orderings is the Vandermonde determinant whose two factors cancel the internal root-difference denominator, so the identity is an integral polynomial identity and specializes to every field. With $p'=pq$ and $U_r=\prod_aQ_{ij}(X_a,y)$, cancellation gives $t_r^{p'}(U_rz)=(-1)^{rA_{ij}}t_{ij}^rt_r^p(z)$, and perfectness of the model forms makes $U_r$ injective on the old quotient. Testing the relative cap against these forms gives $\pi_r\varepsilon_r^{p'}(Q(X_{r+1},y)\operatorname{lift}(z))=(-1)^{A_{ij}}t_{ij}\varepsilon_r^p(z)$ for every nil-Hecke coset element. Normalizing the second maps by the global weight sign $(-1)^{h+1}$ — legitimate because $N$ and $h$ have the same parity and the new $N$ changes by $A_{ij}$ — cancels that sign and gives the exact constant $t_{ij}$; dual-power-basis contraction gives the mixed-unit equation, and reversing colors gives $t_{ji}$ with the stated double-mate ratio. Native minus signs occur twice in these composites, so the scalars persist. [step 2.1, step 3.1, step 5.1, algebra]

7.1 Conclusion. Steps 3.1-6.2 verify every defining relation of [[def-minimal-parabolic-klr-diagram-proof-category]] on the explicit flag modules: the generators and their degrees, both adjunction triangles, the rank-one matrices in both branches with their inverses, the bubble series and slides, the cross-and-cap equations, the mixed isomorphism with its scalars, and the downward $Q$-relations. Monic extensions, their Casimirs, the finite rank-one inverses and the coefficient identities survive arbitrary monic specialization as ungraded maps, and the construction is choice-free. This proves only the formal MODEL relations; faithfulness and the cyclotomic word-corner transfer belong to separate suppliers. [[def-graded-module-and-projective-grothendieck-groups-for-klr-towers]], for
each root degree $\alpha$, finite-dimensional graded left
$R^\Lambda_\alpha$-modules $M$ and finitely generated graded projective $P$ put
$$h_\alpha(P,M):=\operatorname{gdim}\operatorname{HOM}_{R^\Lambda_\alpha}(P,M)=\sum_{d\in\mathbb Z}q^d\dim_k\operatorname{Hom}_{R^\Lambda_\alpha,d}(P,M)\in A .$$
By [[thm-projective-hom-pairing-is-additive-and-graded-sesquilinear]] (whose
finite-dimensional hypotheses hold blockwise) this descends to an
$A$-sesquilinear pairing
$$h:K_0^{\rm gr}(R^\Lambda)\times G_0^{\rm gr}(R^\Lambda)\longrightarrow A,$$
with the twist $q\mapsto q^{-1}$: $h(q^r[P],q^s[M])=q^{s-r}h([P],[M])$. In
particular $h^0(P,S):=\dim_k\operatorname{Hom}^0(P,S)$ is the degree-zero part.
The pairing on the Hecke side is the transported pairing of
[[def-graded-module-and-projective-grothendieck-groups-for-klr-towers]]. Also
fix the two dualities used below: the descended anti-involution $\psi$ of
`def-cyclotomic-klr-diagram-duality-and-graded-module-duals` with its
finite-module duality $D_\psi$ and finite-projective duality $\#$, both

Take $F=\mathbb C$, $\xi=-1$ (so $e=2$), level one $\Lambda_0$ and $d=2$.
Then $H^\Lambda_2=H_{\mathbb C,-1}(S_2)$ with $T_1^2=-2T_1-1$, i.e.
$(T_1+1)^2=0$; the algebra is $\mathbb C[t]/(t^2)$ with $t=T_1+1$, a local
algebra whose unique simple is $D=\mathbb C$ with $t$ acting as $0$, and whose
regular module is the unique indecomposable projective $P=H^\Lambda_2$. Both
partitions of $2$ have content $\alpha_0+\alpha_1$ in the charge-$0$
convention, so $\alpha_0+\alpha_1$ is the only nonzero block and
$H^\Lambda_{\alpha_0+\alpha_1}=\mathbb C[t]/(t^2)$; its transported grading
has $\deg t=2$ (the KLR block is the rank-two $e=2$ block
$F[t]/(t^2)$ with $\deg y_2=2$). The graded Specht modules are the
one-dimensional modules $S(2)=\mathbb C$ and $S(1,1)=\mathbb C$, both with
trivial underlying action of $t$, and the graded composition series of $P$ is
$0\subset tP\subset P$ with $tP\cong D\{2\}$, so
$$[P]=(1+q^2)[D]\quad\text{in }G_0^{\rm gr}(H^\Lambda_{\alpha_0+\alpha_1}),\qquad [P]\notin\{[D],q^{\pm1}[D],\dots\}.$$
The restricted label is $(1,1)$ (since $(1,1)$ is $2$-restricted and $(2)$ is
not), the edge degrees of the two shapes are $\deg(S(1,1))=0$ and
$\deg(S(2))=1$, so the graded Specht classes are $[S(1,1)]=[D]$ and
$[S(2)]=q[D]$, and the level-one Fock data give
$G(1,1)=M_{1,1}+qM_{(2)}$ and $G^*(1,1)=(M_{1,1}+qM_{(2)})/(1+q^2)$; hence
under the transported identifications of
[[thm-ariki-canonical-basis-theorem-in-characteristic-zero]]
$$[P]\longmapsto G(1,1)=M_{1,1}+qM_{(2)}=(1+q^2)G^*(1,1),\qquad [D]\longmapsto G^*(1,1).$$
The graded Cartan pairing of
[[def-graded-cartan-pairing-between-projectives-and-modules]] has
$h([P],[D])=1$ and $h([P],[P])=1+q^2$, while the graded composition
multiplicity is $[P:D]_q=1+q^2$ (ungraded value $2$). Thus the projective class
$[P]$ is not a simple class, and the two bases are dual to each other under $h$
without being equal as classes. All computations are finite and explicit;
choice is inherited only through the transported identifications cited.

[F4] The graded Grothendieck groups, their shift action and the graded Cartan
pairing $h$ are those of
[[def-graded-module-and-projective-grothendieck-groups-for-klr-towers]] and

and simple classes are matched with $G(1,1)$ and $G^*(1,1)$ by
[[thm-ariki-canonical-basis-theorem-in-characteristic-zero]], and the graded
multiplicities by
[[thm-graded-decomposition-numbers-equal-canonical-basis-coefficients-in-characteristic-zero]].

Let $\rho:R\to H$ be an isomorphism of finite-dimensional unital
$\mathbb Z$-graded $k$-algebras. Restriction of scalars along $\rho$ is an
equivalence of graded left module categories which is exact, sends
finite-dimensional modules to finite-dimensional modules, sends a shift
$M\{r\}$ to $M\{r\}$, sends finitely generated graded projectives to finitely
generated graded projectives, preserves composition multiplicities of graded
simples (with shifts), and identifies the graded Hom pairings
$\operatorname{gdim}\operatorname{HOM}$ of
[[def-graded-cartan-pairing-between-projectives-and-modules]]. The inverse equivalence, restriction along $\rho^{-1}$, therefore
induces $A$-module isomorphisms $K_0^{\rm gr}(R)\to K_0^{\rm gr}(H)$ and
$G_0^{\rm gr}(R)\to G_0^{\rm gr}(H)$ intertwining the Cartan homomorphisms and
the forgetful maps $\zeta$.

If moreover $\rho$ intertwines fixed grading-preserving anti-involutions $\ast_R$ and $\ast_H$
(i.e. $\rho(x^{\ast_R})=\rho(x)^{\ast_H}$), then the transported functor
intertwines the two diagram dualities $D_\psi$ and the two projective
Hom-dualities $\#$ of `def-cyclotomic-klr-diagram-duality-and-graded-module-duals`,
and hence preserves normalized self-dual simples and normalized self-dual
indecomposable projectives.

The characteristic-zero theorems of this page
([[thm-ariki-canonical-basis-theorem-in-characteristic-zero]],
[[thm-graded-decomposition-numbers-equal-canonical-basis-coefficients-in-characteristic-zero]])
compute graded decomposition numbers of graded Specht modules as global-basis
coefficients. In characteristic $p>0$ the factorization
[[thm-positive-characteristic-decomposition-polynomials-factor-through-adjustment]]
reduces the graded decomposition matrix to a product of the adjustment matrix
and the SAME global-basis coefficients, but the adjustment matrix is generally
nontrivial: the theorem computes no adjustment entry and asserts no identity
adjustment matrix in general. Consequently the characteristic-zero
canonical-basis theory does not by itself solve the decomposition-number
problem in arbitrary positive characteristic; the general problem retains the
boundary recorded in
[[rem-general-modular-decomposition-numbers-are-not-determined-by-triangularity]]
and [[rem-general-type-a-decomposition-numbers-remain-unsolved]]. This remark
records the boundary; it carries no proof obligation and no choice principle.

The two cited characteristic-zero theorems determine exactly the graded
decomposition numbers in branch (C0), where the transition polynomials
$d_{\lambda,\mu}(q)$ are the global-basis coefficients. The
positive-characteristic factorization leaves the adjustment coefficients
$a_{\lambda,\nu}(q)$ undetermined beyond bar-invariance, nonnegativity, the
diagonal $1$ and the dominance support recorded in
[[def-graded-adjustment-polynomials-in-positive-characteristic]]; consequently
the "same" global-basis coefficients are not by themselves the answer in branch
(CP). The source's announced specialization of the adjustment matrix to the
matrix of James concerns the degenerate parameter and lies outside this page's
nondegenerate regime, as recorded in the batch coverage. No general
positive-characteristic formula is claimed, and this remark is not consumed to
prove any replacement statement. The boundary it states is the same one
recorded in the two unsolved-decomposition-number remarks cited in the
statement.

In branch (CP) of the regime of
[[def-nondegenerate-root-of-unity-level-one-hecke-regime]], for every
$\lambda\in RP_\alpha$ and every partition $\mu$ of content $\alpha$, the
graded decomposition polynomial factors as
$$[S(\mu):D(\lambda)]_q=\sum_{\nu\in RP_\alpha}a_{\lambda,\nu}(q)\,d_{\nu,\mu}(q),$$
where $a_{\lambda,\nu}$ are the adjustment polynomials of
[[def-graded-adjustment-polynomials-in-positive-characteristic]] and
$d_{\nu,\mu}$ the characteristic-independent global-basis transition polynomial
of [[def-level-one-global-basis-transition-polynomials-in-the-symmetric-group-convention]];
equivalently
$[J(\nu)]=[D(\nu)]+\sum_{\lambda\lhd\nu}a_{\lambda,\nu}(q)[D(\lambda)]$. In
particular the characteristic-$p$ decomposition matrix is the product of the
dominance-unitriangular adjustment matrix and the (characteristic-independent)
matrix of global-basis coefficients, and no claim is made that the adjustment
matrix is the identity. Choice is inherited only through the transported
global-basis suppliers.

[F2] The reduced modules satisfy $\Psi_{\rm can}^{\rm Hecke}([J(\nu)])=D_\nu$ over the positive-characteristic field, and the labels agree with the cellular heads in this branch ([[lem-reduction-of-characteristic-zero-simple-modules-modulo-p]], [[lem-positive-characteristic-specht-head-and-cyclotomic-crystal-labels-agree]]).
